To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PLGA-based microparticles can be used as a sustained-release delivery system for anastrozole, a breast cancer drug.

anastrozol-loaded poly(d,1- lactide-co-glycolide) microspheres were successfully formulated by emulsion/extraction technique, and that the microspheres exhibited anastrozole encapsulation efficiencies of 80-90%, and drug release kinetics were best fitted by Higuchi square root of time model.
anastrozol microparticles were successfully prepared by an emulsion/extraction technique, and the drug release from these microparticles followed Higuchi kinetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of biodegradable microparticles of anastrozol, a drug for treatment of breast carcinoma.
the development of a sustained-release formulation of anastrozol microparticles for breast cancer treatment.
the formulation of anastrozol microparticles as anticancer drug carriers and the study of the effect of the drug-polymer interaction and the drug release profile.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLGA microparticle formulation was able to sustain the release of the anticancer drug anastrozole for 2 weeks.
anastrozol-loaded PLGA micoparticles could be a promising alternative to the current delivery methods of the drug.
the anastrozoledrug release kinetics of PLGA microparticals were best described by the Higuchi diffusion model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a sustained release formulation for anastrozole, a potent aromatase inhibitor.
we have successfully formulated anastrozole PLGA microparticle formulation with an average diameter of approximately 5 μm, and the release profile was found to be sustained for more than 100 h.
the anastroxole microparticles could potentially be used as a drug delivery system for breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the drug release kinetics of anastrozol microparticles with poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid), which are used for the treatment of breast cancer, can be controlled by the formulation variables and the release mechanism can be predicted using the dissolution kinetics models.
the anastrozoledrug-loaded microparticles can be used as an effective drug delivery system for the treatment of breast cancer.
the PLGA microparticle formulation of anastrozol can provide an alternative delivery method that can provide a long term treatment for breast cancer.
